text: WiFi card probably will still say, as I turn on my WiFi interface, are you black and white access point there? And clearly there is no black and white access point there because I am at the university. So after the timeout, my WiFi card will try with the second most frequently accessed point I connect to, that is the University Extended Service Center, which is called Poly, right? So it will send a message saying, are you Poly the access point there? And then the Poly access point will answer, okay. So that's typically what manufacturers actually implement in our WiFi cards in order to make the step even faster. So they try first with the most frequently visited access points. They try to contact them. It's not a broadcast. Hello, is there anyone there? Is are you there? Or are you there? Or are you there? And then after some attempts, if nobody of your most frequently accessed points reply, your WiFi card understands that is in a new environment, and then it will send just, is anybody there? Okay, general solicitation. Okay. So the fact that our WiFi card remembers the most, mostly visited, frequently visited access points is good for us, right? Because we get connected very quickly. The step got performed.
